newsitem.title: CANADA: NOVA examines alternative tolling plans.
newsitem.headline: NOVA examines alternative tolling plans.

text.p: NOVA Corp subsidiary NOVA Gas Transmission Ltd, facing the possibility of competition for natural gas transport in Alberta, is making alternative tolling plans for use should new pipelines be built, a NOVA official said on Tuesday.

NOVA Gas Transmission vice president Russ Wells said the company, which currently has a monopoly on moving gas in Alberta, is considering several alternatives -- including zone and distance-based tolls -- to compete with upstart pipelines.
"All of those would be on the table," Wells told reporters at a natural gas conference.

NOVA, which currently moves about 12 billion cubic feet of gas per day in Alberta, faces the prospect of competition from proposed "bypass" pipelines, which include the Palliser Pipeline, co-owned by PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd and Westcoast Energy Inc.

Palliser, which last week submitted its application to Canada's National Energy Board, would carry about 1.2 billion cubic feet of gas per day across the Alberta-Saskatchewan border from just east of Calgary. PanCanadian's production for movement on the line would total 500 million cubic feet per day.
PanCanadian vice president Gerry Protti said on Tuesday the line would bring competition to NOVA, which would benefit all producers by lowering tolls.

The company devised the project because much of its gas production lies between Calgary and Alberta's eastern border. But, under a decades-old toll structure on NOVA, it pays the same to ship its gas on the system as producers in the northernmost regions of the province.

NOVA has contended that the so-called "postage stamp" rate has led to the development of remote gas fields and Alberta's economic growth. All producers currently pay about C$0.26 per thousand cubic feet to ship their gas to the Alberta border from anywhere in the province.

"NOVA has to do what they have to do," Protti said. "All I know is we've got committed shippers and it's going to mean value, not only in terms of the tolls that we're going to provide those shippers, but the value longer-term by having competition."

Wells said opinion on tolls among its 300 customers was mixed, largely depending on the location of their production in Alberta, so discussions with shippers would play a big role in future tariff plans.
"Notwithstanding that, if there is going to be a Palliser Pipeline built then NOVA will be prepared to have a competitive pricing alternative," he said. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
